text: The os and sys modules connect your program to the operating system and the Python runtime.
os lets you interact with the system — here, asking for the current working directory.
It reads environment variables too, like HOME, with a safe default if they're missing.
[chuckle] os dot path joins folder and file names using the correct separator for any operating system.
[sniff] You can list the contents of a directory, walking every file and folder inside it.
That's the foundation for tools that scan, organize, or process files in bulk.
[sigh] sys, by contrast, is about Python itself — its version, the platform it's running on.
And sys dot argv holds the command-line arguments passed to your script, so it can react to user input at launch.
[groan] os and sys are how Python scripts become real tools that read their environment and adapt to it.
